hook: Fire in the hole. Then charge after charge went off.
narration: Fire in the hole. Then this range in Kentucky blew apart, one charge after another.
Combat engineers of the 101st Airborne ran this demolitions range at Fort Campbell on April third, 2019.
They strung barbed wire obstacles, then learned to place explosive charges that destroy that wire fast.
Before every blast the crew shouts fire in the hole, a warning that a charge is about to go off, and everyone gets behind cover.
They also learned to blow deep trenches in the ground, the kind made to stop enemy tanks.
Charge after charge went off across the field, right into the evening.
For the new soldiers, it was their first look at what these charges really do.
outcome: The final charges went off, and the engineers cheered. One said, I love it when a plan comes together.
title: 101st engineers blow up their own range
description:
On April 3, 2019, combat engineers of the 326th Brigade Engineer Battalion, 101st Airborne Division, ran a demolitions range at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, practicing charges that destroy wire obstacles and cut anti-tank trenches.
